field_rationales.category_specs.product_conditioner_reran: A conventional substantive base with ester and oil support is plausibly depositing; no measured finish establishes a high-weight boundary. Low would underrepresent the base plus explicit ester/emollient architecture. High is not justified by a list of oils in an unknown-concentration region; no sensory or repeated-use test resolves richness. Evidence: Cetearyl Alcohol rank3, Isopropyl Palmitate rank4, Behentrimonium Chloride rank5, Oil declarations at ranks8-12. Limit: Formula-only E2: unknown dose, deposition, sensory weight and efficacy. The reviewed keratin route supports comparative temporary film support beyond ordinary lubrication. Low is ordinary conditioning only; hydrolyzed keratin adds the distinct R5 candidate required by v1.6. High needs a materially stronger named bond route; none is declared and the product name/80-percent claim cannot create one. Evidence: Hydrolyzed Keratin in cationic rinse-out conditioner, No named bond chemistry in complete current INCI. Limit: Formula-only E2: unknown dose, deposition, sensory weight and efficacy. Both coherent humectant/emollient conditioning and a distinct hydrolyzed-keratin temporary fibre-film route are visible; balanced is a mixed-architecture decision, not a missing-evidence default. Moisture alone omits the identifiable R5 protein-film candidate in a substantive rinse-out delivery context. Protein dominance is not established by moving keratin earlier in a declaration; robust nonprotein conditioning remains the larger architecture. Evidence: Glycerin rank2 and Panthenol rank6, R1 cationic/fatty-alcohol base with ester and oils, Hydrolyzed Keratin rank7 supplies a distinct R5 candidate. Limit: Formula-only E2: unknown dose, deposition, sensory weight and efficacy. Ingredient flags are deterministic presence signals from the complete normalized INCI: oils, proteins, humectants.
